features.name: oc_engages_op_examples_or_premises
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly engage with a specific example or premise cited in the OP's argument text?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users) and read argument (OP argument text only). Output 1 if at least one single comment explicitly addresses (e.g., quotes, restates, rebuts, questions or builds on) a specific example or premise that is stated in the argument text; generic disagreement with the overall view, or comments that only raise unrelated points, do not count. Output 0 if no comment does so. Empty comment list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments or empty/missing argument gives null. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome in either column as evidence; they cannot establish engagement. Quotation of OP text counts only when the comment goes on to address it rather than merely appearing.

h0: There is no association between oc_engages_op_examples_or_premises and the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Discussions with oc_engages_op_examples_or_premises equal to 1 have a higher probability of view change than those equal to 0.
note: Presence (at least one comment) is assumed for "counter-arguments explicitly engage". Scope is argument text only (not title), per the hypothesis. OLS on binary delta gives a linear probability interpretation; association only. Current text may contain outcome announcements and comment timing is unknown; the semantic spec excludes outcome-related content, but the raw text is not guaranteed pre-outcome.
